en.greeting: Hi! Today we learn words you use every day: clothes, the weather and parts of the body. Small groups of words, one step at a time.

steps.title: Clothes
steps.text: Let's start with clothes. Here are the words you need every day.
steps.body:
Learn these clothes words. **Trousers, jeans** and **shorts** are always plural (treated as 'more than one'), because they have two legs: My jeans **are** new.

For clothes, Indonesian *pakai* is **wear**, not *use*: **She is wearing a red dress.** **Is wearing** = sedang memakai (now). **Wear** = biasa memakai (habit): I wear a uniform every day.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Quick check: which verb goes with clothes?

question.prompt: Look at Pak Hasan. He ___ a batik shirt and black trousers.
question.explanation: For clothes we say **wear**, not use. It's happening now (sedang), so we need **is + -ing**: is wearing. 'Is wear' is missing the -ing.

steps.title: The weather
steps.text: Now the weather. Indonesian just says *Panas*, but an English sentence always needs someone or something at the start, so weather sentences start with **It**. Here *it* doesn't mean anything; it just fills the place.
steps.body:
Say **It's** (= It is) + a weather word: It's sunny, It's hot, It's cloudy.

Rain is a verb (a doing word) here: **It's raining** = sedang hujan. Don't say `Today is rain` or `It's rain`.

To ask, say **What's the weather like?** = Cuacanya bagaimana? Here *like* doesn't mean 'suka'; it's just part of the question.

steps.title: Weather talk
steps.text: Here's how people talk about the weather in real life.
steps.body: Indonesia has a **rainy season** (musim hujan) and a **dry season** (musim kemarau). **It's raining** = now; **it rains every afternoon** = it happens often. **Was** = in the past (kemarin).

examples.en: It's very hot in Jakarta today.
examples.id: Hari ini di Jakarta panas sekali.

examples.en: It's raining, so I'm taking an umbrella.
examples.id: Sedang hujan, jadi saya bawa payung.

examples.en: In the rainy season, it rains every afternoon.
examples.id: Di musim hujan, setiap sore hujan.

examples.en: It's cool and windy in Puncak.
It was cold in Lembang yesterday.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Sari looks out of the window. Choose the right words.

question.prompt: Oh no! It ___ again. Where's my umbrella?
question.explanation: Rain happening now uses **is + -ing** (like 'sedang' in Indonesian): **is raining**. 'It is rain' is a common mistake from Indonesian 'hujan'. *Rains* is for things that happen often, not now.

steps.title: Build the question
steps.text: Now build the weather question.

question.explanation: The weather question is **What is the weather like?** (short: What's the weather like?). **like** goes at the end, and here it doesn't mean 'suka': the whole question just means 'Cuacanya bagaimana?'. Don't say `How is the weather like?`

steps.title: Parts of the body
steps.text: Last group: the body. Two Indonesian words need two English words each.
steps.body:
**Tangan** is **hand** (with fingers) or **arm**. **Kaki** is **foot** (you stand on it) or **leg**.

Two plurals are irregular (they don't add -s, just remember them): one **foot**, two **feet**; one **tooth**, two **teeth**.

One part **hurts**: My back hurts (= it hurts). Two parts **hurt**: My eyes hurt (= they hurt). The -s goes on the verb only for one thing.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Dimas is walking from the station to his office. Help him finish his sentence.

question.explanation: Foot has an irregular plural: one foot, two **feet**. 'Are' tells you it's plural, and 'foots' is not a word.

steps.title: Flashcards
steps.text: Flip through these to review. Say each one out loud.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's everything from today on one page. Keep it handy.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kita belajar kata-kata yang kamu pakai setiap hari: pakaian, cuaca dan bagian tubuh. Sedikit demi sedikit, satu langkah setiap kali.

steps.title: Pakaian
steps.text: Kita mulai dari pakaian. Ini kata-kata yang kamu butuhkan setiap hari.
steps.body:
Pelajari kata-kata pakaian ini. **Trousers, jeans** dan **shorts** selalu jamak (dianggap 'lebih dari satu'), karena kakinya dua: My jeans **are** new.

Untuk pakaian, *pakai* dalam bahasa Inggris adalah **wear**, bukan *use*: **She is wearing a red dress.** **Is wearing** = sedang memakai (sekarang). **Wear** = biasa memakai (kebiasaan): I wear a uniform every day.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Cek cepat: kata kerja apa yang dipakai untuk pakaian?

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Look at Pak Hasan. He ___ a batik shirt and black trousers.
question.explanation: Untuk pakaian kita pakai **wear**, bukan use. Ini terjadi sekarang (sedang), jadi butuh **is + -ing**: is wearing. 'Is wear' tidak punya -ing.

steps.title: Cuaca
steps.text: Sekarang cuaca. Bahasa Indonesia cukup bilang *Panas*, tapi kalimat bahasa Inggris selalu perlu sesuatu di awal, jadi kalimat cuaca dimulai dengan **It**. Di sini *it* tidak punya arti; hanya mengisi tempat.
steps.body:
Katakan **It's** (= It is) + kata cuaca: It's sunny, It's hot, It's cloudy.

Rain di sini kata kerja: **It's raining** = sedang hujan. Jangan bilang `Today is rain` atau `It's rain`.

Untuk bertanya, katakan **What's the weather like?** = Cuacanya bagaimana? Di sini *like* bukan berarti 'suka'; itu cuma bagian dari pertanyaannya.

steps.title: Ngobrol soal cuaca
steps.text: Begini cara orang membicarakan cuaca sehari-hari.
steps.body: Indonesia punya **rainy season** (musim hujan) dan **dry season** (musim kemarau). **It's raining** = sekarang; **it rains every afternoon** = sering terjadi. **Was** = di masa lalu (kemarin).

examples.en: It's very hot in Jakarta today.
examples.id: Hari ini di Jakarta panas sekali.

examples.en: It's raining, so I'm taking an umbrella.
examples.id: Sedang hujan, jadi saya bawa payung.

examples.en: In the rainy season, it rains every afternoon.
examples.id: Di musim hujan, setiap sore hujan.

examples.en: It's cool and windy in Puncak.
It was cold in Lembang yesterday.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Sari melihat ke luar jendela. Pilih kata yang tepat.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Oh no! It ___ again. Where's my umbrella?
question.explanation: Hujan yang sedang turun memakai **is + -ing** (seperti 'sedang' dalam bahasa Indonesia): **is raining**. 'It is rain' adalah kesalahan umum karena kata 'hujan' dalam bahasa Indonesia. *Rains* untuk hal yang sering terjadi, bukan sekarang.

steps.title: Susun pertanyaan
steps.text: Sekarang susun pertanyaan tentang cuaca.

question.explanation: Pertanyaan tentang cuaca adalah **What is the weather like?** (singkatnya: What's the weather like?). **like** ada di akhir, dan di sini tidak berarti 'suka': seluruh pertanyaannya artinya 'Cuacanya bagaimana?'. Jangan bilang `How is the weather like?`

steps.title: Bagian tubuh
steps.text: Kelompok terakhir: tubuh. Ada dua kata Indonesia yang masing-masing punya dua kata Inggris.
steps.body:
**Tangan** bisa **hand** (telapak dan jari) atau **arm** (lengan). **Kaki** bisa **foot** (bagian untuk berdiri) atau **leg**.

Dua bentuk jamak tidak beraturan (tidak pakai -s, hafalkan saja): one **foot**, two **feet**; one **tooth**, two **teeth**.

Satu bagian pakai **hurts**: My back hurts (= it hurts). Dua bagian pakai **hurt**: My eyes hurt (= they hurt). Huruf -s di kata kerja hanya untuk satu benda.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Dimas sedang berjalan dari stasiun ke kantornya. Bantu dia melengkapi kalimatnya.

question.explanation: Foot punya bentuk jamak tidak beraturan: one foot, two **feet**. Kata 'are' menunjukkan jamak, dan 'foots' itu bukan kata.

steps.title: Kartu hafalan
steps.text: Balik kartu-kartu ini untuk mengulang. Ucapkan masing-masing dengan suara keras.

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Ini semuanya dalam satu halaman. Simpan untuk nanti, ya.
